blocks.content:
Articles 168–212 – State Legislature
Assembly – 5 years
Council – Permanent
Minimum age – Assembly 25, Council 30
Money Bill – Assembly only
Governor summons legislature

items: Articles 168–212 deal directly with the State Legislature in competitive exams.
Note the minimum age distinction: Assembly requires 25 years, while Council requires 30 years.
Money Bills are exclusively restricted to the Assembly.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Articles 168–212 pertain to the State Legislature.
The Legislative Assembly serves a 5-year tenure, whereas the Legislative Council is a permanent body.
The minimum age requirement is 25 for the Assembly and 30 for the Council.
Money Bills can be introduced in the Assembly only.
The Governor is responsible for summoning the legislature.
